sentences.en: There is a reasonable assumption we make as we go through life.
sentences.zh: 我们在生活中有一个合理的假设。

sentences.en: Groups act in their own self-intereSt.
sentences.zh: 群体行事总是为了自身的利益。

sentences.en: Merchants sell things in order to make money.
sentences.zh: 商人出售商品是为了赚钱。

sentences.en: Employers want to hire the best employees.
sentences.zh: 雇主想要雇用最好的员工。

sentences.en: Sports teams want to win matches.
The assumption of self-interest is also the lens through which we understand how individuals behave.
sentences.zh: 对自私自利的假设也是我们理解个体行为的视角。

sentences.en: We can see why someone might lie on a resume in order to get ahead.
sentences.zh: 我们可以理解为什么有人会在简历上说谎以求出人头地。

sentences.en: We also know that no one would lie on their resume to make themselves look worse.
sentences.zh: 我们也知道没有人会在简历上说谎让自己看起来更糟糕。

sentences.en: When people are accused of wrongdoing, it makes perfect sense that the guilty would claim to be innocent.
sentences.zh: 当人们被指控做错事时，有罪者声称自己是无辜的完全合乎情理。

sentences.en: But every ounce of common sense tells us no innocent person would ever confess to doing something wrong.
sentences.zh: 但我们的每一点常识都告诉我们，绝没有任何无辜的人会承认自己做了错事。

sentences.en: We understand as a matter of common sense and intuition that people behave in ways that favor their self-intereSt.
sentences.zh: 根据常识和直觉，我们理解人们的行为方式往往符合他们的切身利益。

sentences.en: How in God's name does that favor your self-interest?
sentences.zh: 天哪，这怎么就符合你的切身利益了？

sentences.en: How and why people come to betray their self-interest?
sentences.zh: 人们是如何以及为什么会背叛自己的利益？

sentences.en: In the sixth grade, Saul Kasson received an assignment from his teacher to write a book report.
sentences.zh: 在六年级时，索尔·卡森接到老师布置的一项写读后感的作业。

sentences.en: It took him about a nanosecond to decide to write about his hero, Mickey Mantle.
sentences.zh: 他花了大约纳秒的时间就决定写他的偶像米奇·曼特尔。

sentences.en: I was a huge Yankees fan and I wanted to do a really good job.
sentences.zh: 我是扬基队的超级球迷，我想把这件事做得非常出色。

sentences.en: The baseball star was not the only object of Saul's affections.
sentences.zh: 这位棒球明星并不是索尔倾注喜爱的唯一对象。

sentences.en: His sixth grade teacher was up on a pedestal too.
sentences.zh: 他的六年级老师也被奉上了神坛。

sentences.en: I had a crush, to be honest, on Mrs. Avery.
sentences.zh: 说实话，我对艾弗里太太有点迷恋。

sentences.en: I wanted to impress Mrs. Avery.
sentences.zh: 我想给艾弗里太太留下好印象。

sentences.en: And so I spent a lot of time on this book report.
sentences.zh: 所以我花了很多时间在这篇读后感上。

sentences.en: I just remember being excited to get the grade back.
sentences.zh: 我只记得当时很兴奋地等着拿回成绩。

sentences.en: I thought it was a really good paper.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这是一篇非常好的文章。

sentences.en: I'd spent a lot of time on it.
sentences.zh: 我在上面花了很多时间。

sentences.en: And when she called me up, she would call people and they'd come up and get their paper.
sentences.zh: 当她叫到我时，她会叫大家上去拿他们的作业。

sentences.en: This was toward the end of the school day.
And I just remember her glaring at me in such a way that I looked at the grade.
sentences.zh: 我只记得她怒视着我，以至于我看了看分数。

sentences.en: And there was, with a circle around it, a big red F.
sentences.zh: 上面画着一个圈，里面是一个大大的红色F。

sentences.en: And she says, well, you plagiarized it.
He loved Mrs. Avery and he loved Mickey Mantle.
sentences.zh: 他爱艾弗里太太，也爱米奇·曼特尔。

sentences.en: And he had poured his heart and soul into the book report.
sentences.zh: 他把全部心血都倾注在了这篇读后感上。

sentences.en: I didn't want to break out into tears in front of my classmates and in front of her.
sentences.zh: 我不想在同学们和她面前哭出来。

sentences.en: I got home, flicked open the door.
Mrs. Avery accused me of cheating.
sentences.zh: 艾弗里太太指控我作弊。

sentences.en: She didn't ask me if I plagiarized.
She told me that I did.
And I just will never forget the helplessness that I felt at having been accused of something I didn't do
sentences.zh: 我永远不会忘记那种无助感，因为我被指控做了我没有做的事，

sentences.en: and not really knowing how to respond in a way to defend myself.
sentences.zh: 却不知道该如何回应来为自己辩护。

sentences.en: It was Saul's mother who finally obtained justice.
sentences.zh: 是索尔的母亲最终为他讨回了公道。

sentences.en: She demanded proof from Mrs. Avery that the book report was plagiarized.
sentences.zh: 她要求艾弗里太太证明这篇读后感是抄袭的。

sentences.en: Mrs. Avery looked for evidence but couldn't find any.
sentences.zh: 艾弗里太太寻找证据却找不到任何证据。
于是她改了索尔的成绩。

sentences.en: But the moment of helplessness stayed with Saul.
sentences.zh: 但那种无助的时刻一直留在索尔心中。

sentences.en: Why had he been unable to speak up?
sentences.zh: 为什么他当时无法开口说话？

sentences.en: Saul grew up to become a psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 索尔长大后成为了一名心理学家。

sentences.en: How people interpret the actions of others.
sentences.zh: 人们如何解读他人的行为。

sentences.en: He was especially fascinated by juries.
Here were people whose conclusions about defendants had life and death stakes.
sentences.zh: 这里的人们对被告所下的结论关乎生死存亡。

sentences.en: To evaluate the psychological factors that shape how juries think,
sentences.zh: 为了评估塑造陪审团思维的心理因素，

sentences.en: Saul came up with cases where some jurors might feel a defendant was guilty,
sentences.zh: 索尔设计了一些案件，在这些案件中，一些陪审员可能会觉得被告有罪，

sentences.en: while others might feel he was innocent.
sentences.zh: 而另一些人可能会觉得他是无辜的。

sentences.en: Saul figured ambiguous cases would shed light on how people make up their minds about guilt and innocence.
sentences.zh: 索尔认为，模棱两可的案件将有助于阐明人们是如何对有罪与无罪做出决定的。

sentences.en: He started running experiments with volunteers playing the role of jurors.
sentences.zh: 他开始用扮演陪审员的志愿者进行实验。

sentences.en: He noticed there were some cases where his volunteers were totally unanimous.
sentences.zh: 他注意到有些案件他的志愿者意见完全一致。

sentences.en: A couple of cases came back that elicited no variability.
sentences.zh: 有几个案件的反馈没有任何变数。

sentences.en: As far as everybody was concerned, everybody was guilty.
sentences.zh: 在所有人看来，每个人都是有罪的。

sentences.en: Fortunately, we also asked subjects in those studies to explain their verdict.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，我们还要求这些研究中的受试者解释他们的裁决。

sentences.en: What was the basis for your verdict?
sentences.zh: 你们作出裁决的依据是什么？

sentences.en: And in the cases that I recall, everybody cited a confession.
sentences.zh: 在我记得的案件中，所有人都提到了供词。

sentences.en: When a defendant in a criminal case admitted he had done something wrong,
sentences.zh: 当刑事案件中的被告承认自己做了错事时，

sentences.en: volunteers playing the role of jurors saw these as open and shut cases.
sentences.zh: 扮演陪审员角色的志愿者认为这些都是板上钉钉的案件。

sentences.en: My first response was, well, that's interesting.
sentences.zh: 我的第一反应是，嗯，这很有趣。

sentences.en: It looks like we'll have to remove confessions from evidence in order to use cases.
sentences.zh: 看来我们必须从证据中排除供词，才能使用这些案件。

sentences.en: Saul wanted cases where volunteers disagreed with each other.
sentences.zh: 索尔想要志愿者意见不一的案件。

sentences.en: Cases involving confessions, where everyone agreed with everyone else, were useless.
sentences.zh: 涉及供词且所有人意见一致的案件毫无用处。

sentences.en: So right away, we tossed out cases involving confessions because confessions were a nuisance.
sentences.zh: 所以我们立刻抛弃了涉及供词的案件，因为供词是个干扰项。

sentences.en: It happens so often in science as well as in life.
sentences.zh: 这在科学中和生活中经常发生。

sentences.en: We fail to notice something important because we are so intent on something else.
sentences.zh: 我们因为过于专注于某事而未能注意到重要的事情。

sentences.en: It took Saul a while to realize his nuisance was telling him something important.
sentences.zh: 索尔花了点时间才意识到他的干扰项正在告诉他一些重要的事情。

sentences.en: As he continued to study juries, Saul decided he needed to better understand how police procured
sentences.zh: 随着他对陪审团研究的深入，索尔决定他需要更好地了解警察如何在刑事审判中获取

sentences.en: He decided to audit a law school class on evidence.
sentences.zh: 他决定旁听一门法学院的证据学课程。

sentences.en: And there was a footnote in that casebook in which they referenced an interrogation manual,
sentences.zh: 在那本案例汇编里有一个脚注，里面提到了一本审讯手册，

sentences.en: So I thought, wow, how interesting to see what they're doing to interrogate.
sentences.zh: 所以我想，哇，看看他们在审讯中做什么，太有趣了。

sentences.en: And so I went to the library and pulled out that edition of that manual, and I read the book.
sentences.zh: 于是我去了图书馆，翻出了那版手册，并读了这本书。

sentences.en: What kind of techniques were in this manual, Saul?
sentences.zh: 这本手册里有什么样的技术，索尔？

sentences.en: Well, for starters, the opening salvo of an interrogation was to bring in a suspect
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，审讯的开场白就是把嫌疑人带进来，

sentences.en: and declare an accusation of guilt.
This, of course, is exactly what Mrs. Avery had done in the sixth grade.
sentences.zh: 这当然正是艾弗里太太在六年级时做过的事。

sentences.en: In fact, I believe in that first manual, they advised the interrogator to come in with a
sentences.zh: 事实上，我相信在第一本手册中，他们建议审讯人员带着装满

sentences.en: folder full of materials and toss it on the table and said, we've got a lot of evidence
sentences.zh: 材料的文件夹走进来，把它扔在桌上说，我们有大量对你不利的证据

sentences.en: And they suggested doing that even if you didn't have a whole lot of evidence.
sentences.zh: 他们建议即使你没有那么多证据也要这样做。

sentences.en: So right out of the gate, I'm looking and I'm saying, okay, wow, these are powerful tactics.
sentences.zh: 所以一开始我就在看，然后我说，好吧，哇，这些都是强力战术。
这些简直带有米格尔姆式的色彩。

sentences.en: In the early 1960s, Stanley Milgram conducted a series of experiments on blind obedience.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪60年代初，斯坦利·米格尔姆进行了一系列关于盲目服从的实验。

sentences.en: He tested if volunteers would comply with instructions from an authority figure.
sentences.zh: 他测试志愿者是否会听从权威人物的指令。

sentences.en: The most famous experiment featured an experimenter who demanded that a volunteer subject someone
sentences.zh: 最著名的实验涉及一位实验人员，他要求志愿者对其他人实施

sentences.en: In reality, no one received shocks.
sentences.zh: 实际上，没有人受到电击。

sentences.en: The experiment was designed to test if volunteers were willing to go along with crazy instructions.
sentences.zh: 该实验旨在测试志愿者是否愿意执行疯狂的指令。

sentences.en: If the volunteer resisted, the experimenter had a series of verbal prods to keep the experiment
sentences.zh: 如果志愿者抵抗，实验人员有一系列言语催促来让实验

sentences.en: It's absolutely essential that you continue.
sentences.zh: 你继续下去绝对是至关重要的。

sentences.en: You have no other choice, teacher.
The experiment requires that you continue.
And the prods are designed to get a subject to first administer a 15-volt shock and then
sentences.zh: 这些催促旨在让受试者首先施加15伏的电击，然后

sentences.en: a 30-volt shock and in 15-volt increments to bring that subject up to the point where they
sentences.zh: 施加30伏的电击，以15伏的增量使该受试者达到被要求施加450伏电击的程度，

sentences.en: would be asked to administer a 450-volt shock, which on Milgram's shock machine was listed as
sentences.zh: 在米格尔姆的电击机上，这被列为

sentences.en: When you look at this paradigm, you go, nobody's going to do that.
sentences.zh: 当你看到这种范式时，你会想，没人会这么做。

sentences.en: Well, I'm not going on a few years users to do it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不打算……有些用户会这么做。

sentences.en: The experiment requires that you go on, teacher.
Sixty-five percent of subjects go all the way up the shock scale to 450 volts.
sentences.zh: 百分之六十五的受试者一直把电击等级拉到450伏。

sentences.en: Now I look at the interrogation manual.
You bring them in, isolated, no friends or family members or lawyers present.
sentences.zh: 你把他们带进来，隔离起来，没有朋友、家人或律师在场。

sentences.en: There is, instead of an experimenter as an authority figure, a police detective who has
sentences.zh: 取代作为权威人物的实验人员的，是一名拥有

sentences.en: And that police detective aims to accuse you of something and get you to make an admission
sentences.zh: 而这位警察侦探的目标是控告你某事并让你承认

sentences.en: And through a process of gradual escalation and a series of prods that are listed, the detective's
sentences.zh: 通过逐步升级的过程和列出的一系列催促，侦探的

sentences.en: goal is to get you to make a small confession or an admission of, I was there.
sentences.zh: 目标是让你做一个小小的招认或承认“我在现场”。

sentences.en: And then a slightly greater admission.
sentences.zh: 然后是稍微多一点的承认。

sentences.en: And then a slightly greater admission.
sentences.zh: 然后是更多一点的承认。

sentences.en: And eventually, 15 volts at a time, the goal is to get that person to make a full admission
sentences.zh: 最终，每次15伏，其目标是让这个人做出完全的有罪招认，

sentences.en: of guilt, coupled by a full narrative confession that explains the chronology and the story.
sentences.zh: 并配有一份解释时间线和故事的完整叙述性供词。

sentences.en: The authority figure in Milgram's obedience experiment, it's a psychology experimenter wearing a white
sentences.zh: 米格尔姆服从实验中的权威人物，是一个穿着白色

sentences.en: lab coat who has no real authority and no real power over those subjects.
sentences.zh: 实验服的心理学实验员，他对这些受试者没有真正的权威，也没有真正的权力。

sentences.en: If an authority figure like a psych experimenter can produce that level of obedience, can you
sentences.zh: 如果像心理学实验员这样的权威人物能产生这种程度的服从，你能

sentences.en: imagine what a detective who has power over your fate and future might be able to produce?
sentences.zh: 想象一个对你的命运和未来拥有权力的侦探能够产生什么结果吗？
这就是让我感到不安的地方。

sentences.en: I kept thinking, geez, if they bring innocent people into this situation, they're going to
sentences.zh: 我一直在想，天哪，如果他们把无辜的人带入这种境地，他们
会得到类似米格尔姆实验的结果。

sentences.en: Saul realized he was confronting two powerful facts.
sentences.zh: 索尔意识到他正在面对两个强有力的人事实。

sentences.en: Fact number one, juries believe people when they offer confessions.
sentences.zh: 事实一，陪审团在听到招供时往往会相信当事人。

sentences.en: Fact number two, police are taught to extract confessions from people using a series of powerful
sentences.zh: 事实二，警方受过专门培训，会通过一系列强有力的

sentences.en: You don't have to assume bad intent on the part of detectives for this to be a problem.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说你必须假设侦探有什么恶意的动机。

sentences.en: Like the rest of us, detectives assume no one who is innocent will
sentences.zh: 和我们其他人一样，侦探们也会理所当然地认为，没有哪个无辜的人会

sentences.en: Saul decided to look more closely at the science of confessions.
sentences.zh: 索尔决定更深入地研究关于招供的科学。

sentences.en: Only, he found, there was no science of confessions.
sentences.zh: 然而他发现，根本没有什么招供科学。

sentences.en: When someone says they did something wrong, it seems so self-evidently obvious that they did
sentences.zh: 当某人承认自己做错了事时，事情看起来如此显而易见，仿佛他们确实

sentences.en: do something wrong that no one had really studied it.
sentences.zh: 做错了事，以至于根本没有人真正去研究过这个课题。

sentences.en: Saul did find one early example, though, a case study described in the early 20th century
sentences.zh: 不过，索尔确实找到了一个早期的例子，那是20世纪初

sentences.en: by a psychologist named Hugo Munsterberg.
sentences.zh: 由一位名叫雨果·芒斯特伯格的心理学家所描述的一个案例研究。

sentences.en: Munsterberg has a chapter titled Untrue Confessions, and in it, he describes this case out of Chicago,
sentences.zh: 芒斯特伯格有一章的标题叫做《不真实的供词》，他在其中描述了芝加哥发生的一起案件，
即贝茜·霍利斯特谋杀案。

sentences.en: What was interesting and what I think made him skeptical about the confession was, first
sentences.zh: 有趣的地方，也是我认为让他对那份供词产生怀疑的原因在于，首先，

sentences.en: of all, the suspect whom confessed had limited cognitive abilities and was a vulnerable person
sentences.zh: 招供的嫌疑人认知能力有限，作为一个嫌疑人来说，
他属于极为弱势的人群。

sentences.en: He then realized that they then brought him in for hours of interrogation, in which it was
sentences.zh: 然后他意识到，警方对嫌疑人进行了长达数小时的审讯，

sentences.en: described that he embellished a story from one telling to another.
sentences.zh: 据描述，他在讲述时不断添枝加叶，前后说法不一。

sentences.en: Turns out he provided some details in that story, and it turns out that some of those details
sentences.zh: 结果证明，他在讲述中提供了一些细节，而且事实证明，其中一些细节

sentences.en: And so we have a situation where he was interrogated for long periods of time.
sentences.zh: 因此，这就出现了一种情况：他受到了长时间的审讯。

sentences.en: He was a vulnerable suspect, and the confession he gave was not particularly accurate in relation
sentences.zh: 他是一个处于弱势的嫌疑人，并且他所作出的供词与案件的实际事实

sentences.en: And yet, the prosecutor pushed forward, and within, I kid you not, one week, he was convicted.
sentences.zh: 然而，检察官却执意推进案件，说实话，不到一个星期，他就被定罪了。

sentences.en: And shortly thereafter, he was hung.
sentences.zh: 没过多久，他就被绞死了。

sentences.en: Saul started looking for other cases of untrue confessions in the history books.
sentences.zh: 索尔开始在历史书籍中寻找其他关于不实供词的案例。

sentences.en: Eventually, he came up with a classification system.
sentences.zh: 最终，他提出了一套分类系统。

sentences.en: The first kind were voluntary false confessions, like the time in 1932 when a famous aviator's
sentences.zh: 第一种是主动型虚假供词，就像1932年那位著名飞行员的
儿子遭到绑架的那次事件一样。

sentences.en: Charles Lindbergh was at the time an American hero, and his infant son was kidnapped.
sentences.zh: 查尔斯·林德伯格当时是美国的英雄，而他幼小的儿子却被绑架了。

sentences.en: And it was big news, as you can imagine, and 200 people volunteered confessions to that
sentences.zh: 你可以想象，这成为了轰动全国的大新闻，有200人主动跑到警察局
承认自己实施了那起绑架。

sentences.en: And ultimately, police did not charge any of them.
sentences.zh: 最终，警方没有对他们中的任何人提出指控。

sentences.en: Ultimately, none of them had anything to do with it.
sentences.zh: 说到底，他们当中没有一个人与那起案件有关。

sentences.en: It's interesting, to some extent ironic, that when someone volunteers a confession, police
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，甚至在某种程度上具有讽刺意味的是，当有人主动招供时，警察

sentences.en: are inherently suspicious, and they look for proof of guilt to corroborate that voluntary
sentences.zh: 往往会天然地产生怀疑，并寻找能够证明有罪的证据来佐证

sentences.en: So they might ask, for example, for facts.
sentences.zh: 所以他们可能会要求对方提供事实依据。

sentences.en: Okay, you say you committed this crime.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你说你犯了这个罪。

sentences.en: Tell me about the case facts.
Describe the crime scene to me, or lead me to the weapon, or lead me to the victim.
sentences.zh: 向我描述一下犯罪现场，或者带我去找凶器，或者带我去找受害者。

sentences.en: And invariably, innocent, voluntary false confessors can't do it.
sentences.zh: 而无辜的主动虚假供述者往往根本做不到这一点。

sentences.en: Voluntary false confessions are cases in which innocent people, without any external pressure
sentences.zh: 主动型虚假供词是指在没有任何来自警方的外部压力的情况下，

sentences.en: from police step forward and confess to crimes they didn't commit.
sentences.zh: 无辜的人主动站出来，承认自己并未犯下的罪行。
有时他们是为了保护其他人。

sentences.en: It might be a child covering for a parent, or a parent covering for a child.
sentences.zh: 可能是孩子为了掩护父母，或者是父母为了掩护孩子。

sentences.en: So sometimes it's a, you know, sort of a rational reason like that.
sentences.zh: 所以有时候，你知道的，这是一种诸如此类的理性动机。

sentences.en: And then sometimes it's a reason that reeks of pathology and somebody needing to gain attention.
sentences.zh: 但有时这种动机充满了病态色彩，纯粹是出于吸引他人注意的需要。

sentences.en: The motives may vary, but it is my sense that voluntary false confessions don't present much of a problem for the criminal justice system.
sentences.zh: 动机可能各不相同，但我的直觉是，主动型虚假供词并不会给刑事司法系统带来太大的麻烦。

sentences.en: So a second kind of false confession is something that you've termed compliant confessions.
sentences.zh: 那么第二种虚假供词，就是你所说的顺从型供词。

sentences.en: And as you started to look at the historical record, you find quite a few examples of this,
sentences.zh: 当你开始查看历史记录时，你会发现这类例子的确不少，

sentences.en: sometimes going back decades or even centuries.
sentences.zh: 有时甚至可以追溯到几十年甚至几个世纪前。

sentences.en: You tell the story about events that took place in the 17th century, for example, in Salem.
sentences.zh: 比如，你讲述了发生在17世纪塞勒姆的事件。

sentences.en: Yeah, the Salem witch trials are a great example.
sentences.zh: 是的，塞勒姆审巫案就是一个极好的例子。

sentences.en: Compliant false confessions, these are cases where somebody is under great amounts of stress.
sentences.zh: 顺从型虚假供词，指的是当事人承受着巨大压力的情况。

sentences.en: They are motivated to put an end to that stress.
sentences.zh: 他们有着摆脱这种压力的强烈动机。

sentences.en: They want out of that bad situation.
sentences.zh: 他们只想离开那个糟糕的处境。

sentences.en: They're not even thinking about long-term consequences.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至不会去考虑长期的后果。

sentences.en: They may have come to believe it's in their better interest to confess than to deny involvement.
sentences.zh: 他们可能已经开始相信，招供比否认参与更符合他们的最大利益。

sentences.en: They know they're innocent, but they confess anyway as a way to get out of a bad situation.
sentences.zh: 他们明知自己是无辜的，但为了摆脱糟糕的处境，还是选择了招供。

sentences.en: Those types of cases go back throughout history.
sentences.zh: 这类案件贯穿了整个人类历史。

sentences.en: In the Salem witch trials, some suspects who failed to confess were executed.
sentences.zh: 在塞勒姆审巫案中，一些拒绝招供的嫌疑人被处以极刑。

sentences.en: Given the choice between making a false confession and being put to death, many chose to lie about their guilt.
sentences.zh: 在作出虚假供词和被处死之间进行选择时，许多人选择在是否有罪这件事上说谎。

sentences.en: Of course, the Salem witch trials took place over 300 years ago.
sentences.zh: 当然，塞勒姆审巫案发生于300多年前。

sentences.en: The same thing couldn't happen today, could it?
sentences.zh: 同样的事情今天不可能发生，对吧？

sentences.en: You know, I was teaching at Williams College.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，当时我正在威廉姆斯学院教书。

sentences.en: It's a liberal arts college in Massachusetts.
sentences.zh: 那是一所位于马萨诸塞州的文理学院。

sentences.en: And I was preparing for classes in the fall.
sentences.zh: 我正在为秋季学期的课程做准备。

sentences.en: And this producer called and said, I wonder if you can look at some confessions for us.
sentences.zh: 这时有个制片人打电话来说，不知道你能不能帮我们看看一些供词。

sentences.en: I said, OK, what's the case?
And she said, will you promise not to mention this to anyone?
sentences.zh: 她说，你答应我绝不把这事告诉任何人，行吗？

sentences.en: And I said, sure, it's confidential.
sentences.zh: 我说，没问题，这是保密的。

sentences.en: And she said, it's the Central Park jogger.
sentences.zh: 她说，是中央公园慢跑者案。

sentences.en: When we come back, the story of the Central Park jogger.
sentences.zh: 广告之后，为您讲述中央公园慢跑者案的故事。
您正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: A quick word before we start this next segment.
sentences.zh: 在进入下一个板块之前，先简要说明一下。

sentences.en: We're going to be discussing two violent crimes that psychologist Saul Kasson has studied.
sentences.zh: 我们将要讨论的是心理学家索尔·卡森所研究的两起暴力犯罪案件。

sentences.en: These cases include graphic accounts of murder and rape.
sentences.zh: 这些案件包含关于谋杀和强奸的血腥描述。

sentences.en: one evening in April 1989, a 28-year-old woman was attacked while taking a run in Central Park in New York.
sentences.zh: 1989年4月的一个晚上，一名28岁的女子在纽约中央公园慢跑时遭到袭击。

sentences.en: She was beaten, raped, and left for dead.
sentences.zh: 她遭到殴打、强奸，并被凶手认为必死无疑而遗弃在现场。

sentences.en: Around 1.30 a.m., she was found unconscious by two passersby.
sentences.zh: 大约凌晨1点30分，两名路人发现了昏迷不醒的她。

sentences.en: She was rushed to the hospital, where she remained in a coma for 12 days.
sentences.zh: 她被紧急送往医院，并在昏迷状态中度过了12天。

sentences.en: Psychologist Saul Kasson remembers the news stories about the horrific crime.
sentences.zh: 心理学家索尔·卡森还记得当时关于这起骇人听闻的罪行的种种新闻报道。

sentences.en: For a city that was already on edge, this was the breaking point.
sentences.zh: 对于一座已经处于高度紧张边缘的城市来说，这就是压垮骆驼的最后一根稻草。

sentences.en: The papers were just filled with headlines that, you know, we've got to solve this.
sentences.zh: 各大报纸的头条全都在说，你知道的，我们必须破案。

sentences.en: I understand fully that when this happened, and when it was reported, and the heinousness of the crime,
sentences.zh: 我完全理解，当这起案件发生时，当媒体进行报道时，鉴于罪行的极其残暴，

sentences.en: the city was in a state of outrage and demanding that we find who did this.
sentences.zh: 整个城市都陷入了愤怒之中，并强烈要求找出真凶。

sentences.en: Within 72 hours, NYPD solved the case.
sentences.zh: 在72小时内，纽约市警察局就破了案。

sentences.en: There were a number of kids running through the park that night, wreaking havoc on some bystanders,
sentences.zh: 那天晚上有许多孩子在公园里奔跑，对路人进行滋扰破坏，

sentences.en: and police immediately started rounding people up, going into their neighborhoods, bringing others in.
sentences.zh: 警方随即开始四处抓人，进入他们的社区，把其他人带回警局。

sentences.en: They interrogated all sorts of kids, and ultimately found five kids who confessed, 14, 15, 16 years old.
sentences.zh: 他们审讯了各种各样的孩子，最终找到了五个招供的孩子，他们的年龄分别是14、15、16岁。
所有人都是黑人或拉丁裔。

sentences.en: Police questioned them for hours and got their confessions, including four on videotape.
sentences.zh: 警方对他们进行了数小时的盘问并得到了口供，其中有四人的招供过程被录成了视频。

sentences.en: The way New York City worked their confessions in those days, starting in the 1970s, 1980s,
sentences.zh: 从20世纪70、80年代开始，纽约市警方在当时记录口供的方式是，

sentences.en: was the detectives interrogated off camera.
sentences.zh: 侦探们在镜头之外进行审讯。

sentences.en: They brought their suspect to a point where they were ready to confess,
sentences.zh: 他们将嫌疑人审讯到准备招供的阶段，

sentences.en: and then they delivered them to an assistant district attorney,
sentences.zh: 然后将他们交由助理地区检察官，

sentences.en: who stepped in, with a camera on, and took the confession.
sentences.zh: 后者会走进审讯室，在摄像机开启的情况下录取口供。

sentences.en: Would you please tell us what your full name is?
sentences.zh: 请告诉我们你的全名叫什么？
亚伦·特朗普、拉蒙特·麦克雷。

sentences.en: Would you please state your full name?

sentences.zh: 卡莉·贾米拉·波恩特-恩-维斯。
zh_words: 卡莉·贾米拉·波恩特-恩-维斯

sentences.en: Hey, would you please sit up and tell me what your name is?
sentences.zh: 嘿，请坐起来，告诉我你叫什么名字？

sentences.en: I'm sorry, you have to speak a little louder.
They described the jogger as she was running.
sentences.zh: 他们描述了慢跑者跑步时的情形。
他们描述了她所在的位置。

sentences.en: They described dragging her down through the grass.
sentences.zh: 他们描述了将她拖进草地的情景。
现场留下了清晰的鞋底印记。

sentences.en: And they gave a description of a woman who had been beaten in the head with a hard object,
sentences.zh: 他们描述了一个女人头部遭到硬物击打，

sentences.en: closed, pulled off, and left for dead.
sentences.zh: 衣物被脱掉，并被丢弃等死的情形。

sentences.en: You cannot look past those statements on video.
sentences.zh: 你无法忽视视频中的那些陈述。

sentences.en: They got some of the facts right.
sentences.zh: 他们确实说对了一些事实。

sentences.en: They're basically telling the same story.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上讲述的是同一个故事。

sentences.en: There are some annoying disparities and contradictions between them.
sentences.zh: 他们之间存在一些令人费解的出入和矛盾。

sentences.en: But they get enough facts right.
sentences.zh: 但他们说对的事实足够多。

sentences.en: None of the boys had attorneys present.
sentences.zh: 所有男孩在受审时都没有律师在场。

sentences.en: In the video confession of 16-year-old Corey Wise, he's sitting in what looks like a classroom.
sentences.zh: 在16岁的小科里·怀斯的视频供词中，他坐在一间看起来像教室的地方。

sentences.en: His knees are shaking with nervous energy.
sentences.zh: 他的膝盖因为紧张而止不住地颤抖。

sentences.en: A prosecutor grills him with questions.
sentences.zh: 检察官连珠炮似地向他提出各种问题。

sentences.en: Where do you go to school?
And what grade are you in there?
He said he was involved in the rape.
He was present and he played a minimal role.
sentences.zh: 他在现场并且起到了很小的作用。

sentences.en: I believe he said he had held her legs while someone else pulled her pants down.
sentences.zh: 我记得他说过，当别人脱下她的裤子时，他按住了她的腿。

sentences.en: I wasn't doing as much as they was doing.
sentences.zh: 我当时做的事没他们那么多。

sentences.en: Were you going up to her crotch?
sentences.zh: 你当时有靠近她的裤裆吗？

sentences.en: I could see the expression on her face that I felt kind of bad.
sentences.zh: 我能看到她脸上的表情，这让我觉得有点糟糕。

sentences.en: This is my first treatment I did to any type of female on the street.
sentences.zh: 这是我第一次对街上的任何女性下手。

sentences.en: When you hear a statement like that, he not only describes what happened, but then describes
sentences.zh: 当你听到这样的陈述时，他不仅描述了发生的事情，还描述了

sentences.en: I'm sorry I did this, he basically said.
sentences.zh: 他基本上说，我很抱歉我做了这些。

sentences.en: It's going to be my laSt.
This is going to be my last time doing it.
sentences.zh: 这将是我最后一次做这种事。
所以当我那样做的时候。

sentences.en: Here's a confession that's not just communicating an admission of guilt and some narrative details
sentences.zh: 这是一个供述，它不仅传达了认罪和一些叙述细节

sentences.en: that are accurate in relation to the crime facts.
sentences.zh: 这些细节与犯罪事实是相符的。

sentences.en: But now he's reflecting on his own motivation and remorse and acceptance of responsibility.
sentences.zh: 而且现在他还在反思自己的动机、悔意和责任感。

sentences.en: How does a judge and a jury look past that statement?
sentences.zh: 法官和陪审团怎么能忽视这样的供述呢？

sentences.en: And when you have four of them, even though they don't align with each other perfectly,
sentences.zh: 当你拥有四个这样的供述时，尽管它们彼此并不完全吻合，

sentences.en: how can a jury look past those four statements?
sentences.zh: 陪审团怎么能忽视这四个供述呢？
所有五名青少年都被定罪了。

sentences.en: For several years, most everyone thought they were guilty.
sentences.zh: 好几年里，几乎所有人都认为他们有罪。

sentences.en: The convictions continued to gnaw at Saul, however.
sentences.zh: 然而，这些定罪一直折磨着索尔。

sentences.en: And then one day, he got a call from ABC News.
sentences.zh: 直到有一天，他接到了美国广播公司的电话。

sentences.en: The producer said ABC had received a tip that the teenager's confessions were made up.
sentences.zh: 制片人说美国广播公司收到一条线索，称这些青少年的供述是捏造的。

sentences.en: And so they sent me two big Xerox-type boxes.
sentences.zh: 于是他们给我寄了两个大号的施乐复印件纸箱。

sentences.en: And I spent the next couple of weeks probably doing terrible teaching at Williams
sentences.zh: 接下来的几周里，我在威廉姆斯的教学大概糟透了

sentences.en: because I was completely distracted by this case.
sentences.zh: 因为我完全被这个案子分心了。

sentences.en: And when I was done, I was horrified.
There was no evidence of their guilt.
sentences.zh: 没有任何证据证明他们有罪。

sentences.en: What were some of the details, if you remember it, that actually were at odds with one another?
sentences.zh: 如果你还记得的话，有哪些细节实际上是互相矛盾的？

sentences.en: And this is the complicated thing because sometimes, of course,
sentences.zh: 这就是复杂的地方，因为有时候，当然，

sentences.en: you know, if you have three eyewitnesses at a scene of anything that happens, a traffic crash,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如果在任何事件现场有三个目击证人，比如一场交通事故，

sentences.en: they, in fact, are not going to agree.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们的说法是不会一致的。

sentences.en: In fact, there's a wealth of psychological studies that show that they will not agree on all of the details.
sentences.zh: 事实上，大量的心理学研究表明，他们在所有细节上都不会达成一致。

sentences.en: And, in fact, they might come up with important discrepancies.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们可能会出现重大的分歧。

sentences.en: And in some ways, it's suspicious if five people at the scene of a traffic crash describe it perfectly.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，如果交通事故现场的五个人描述得完美无缺，反倒可疑了。

sentences.en: So there's a part of you that thinks some of these discrepancies might actually be because people forget.
sentences.zh: 所以你心里会觉得，其中一些分歧实际上可能是因为人们忘记了。

sentences.en: So it's actually not surprising that some things might clash with one another.
sentences.zh: 所以有些事情彼此冲突其实并不奇怪。

sentences.en: And I think that's what everyone was thinking.
sentences.zh: 我想这也是当时所有人的想法。

sentences.en: I didn't know this in 1989, but I learned in 2002 that detectives showed Corey Wise pictures of the victim.
sentences.zh: 我在1989年不知道这一点，但在2002年我了解到，侦探向科里·怀斯展示了受害者的照片。

sentences.en: So he was able to describe her.
He was taken to the crime scene.
He gave a vivid description of the crime scene.
sentences.zh: 他对犯罪现场进行了生动的描述。

sentences.en: Turns out two of them were taken to the crime scene.
sentences.zh: 结果证明其中两人被带去了犯罪现场。
这简直是在污染他们的记忆。

sentences.en: That's now, this is not their statement.
sentences.zh: 这下子，这根本不是他们自己的供述了。

sentences.en: You've motivated and incentivized them because they think it's in their best interest to cooperate.
sentences.zh: 你激励并诱导了他们，因为他们认为合作最符合他们的最大利益。

sentences.en: And you've spoon-fed them information to provide a compelling, accurate confession.
sentences.zh: 而你却一直在向他们灌输信息，以提供一份令人信服且准确的供述。

sentences.en: Nobody expected a full alignment of all the facts.
sentences.zh: 没有人期望所有事实能完全吻合。

sentences.en: And that's why I think the judges and juries, they were convicted at two different trials,
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我认为法官和陪审团——他们是在两次不同的审判中被定罪的——

sentences.en: were able to look past those discrepancies.
The judges and jurors in the trials behaved exactly like the volunteers in Saul's early jury experiments.
sentences.zh: 审判中的法官和陪审员的表现，与索尔早期陪审团实验中的志愿者如出一辙。

sentences.en: It didn't matter that there was compelling evidence pointing in another direction.
sentences.zh: 指向另一个方向的强劲证据根本不重要。

sentences.en: There were several semen samples taken, sent to the FBI lab.
sentences.zh: 警方提取了几个精液样本，并送往联邦调查局实验室。

sentences.en: That summer, the results came back.
First, all of those samples taken trace back to one person.
sentences.zh: 首先，所有这些样本都追溯到同一个人。

sentences.en: That person was not one of those five confessors.
sentences.zh: 那个人并不是那五个招供的人之一。

sentences.en: We have two juries in which they are told that they confessed on the one hand,
sentences.zh: 我们有两个陪审团，一方面他们被告知这些人招供了，

sentences.en: but they're excluded by the DNA on the other.
sentences.zh: 但另一方面DNA检测又排除了他们。

sentences.en: And as one of the jurors said in an interview years later,
sentences.zh: 正如其中一位陪审员在多年后的采访中所说，

sentences.en: they had a confession, and if there's a confession, what else do you need to know?
sentences.zh: 他们有一份供述，既然有了供述，你还想知道什么？

sentences.en: ABC News contacted Saul because a previously convicted criminal
sentences.zh: 美国广播公司联系索尔是因为此前一名被定罪的罪犯

sentences.en: had come forward to claim responsibility for the crime.
sentences.zh: 站出来声称对这起罪行负责。

sentences.en: A serial rapist named Matias Reyes said he was the one who had attacked the Central Park jogger.
sentences.zh: 一名叫马蒂亚斯·雷耶斯的连环强奸犯自称是袭击中央公园慢跑者的凶手。

sentences.en: The samples taken from the crime scene matched his DNA.
sentences.zh: 从犯罪现场提取的样本与他的DNA相符。

sentences.en: In December of 2002, their convictions were overturned.
The DA's office filed a motion to overturn the convictions,
sentences.zh: 地方检察官办公室提交了一项推翻定罪的动议，

sentences.en: and the judge agreed with that motion, and so there were convictions overturned.
sentences.zh: 法官批准了该动议，因此定罪被撤销了。

sentences.en: The city eventually paid the boys $41 million for the mistake
and for the suffering that they had inflicted on them.
sentences.zh: 以及给他们带来的痛苦，市政府最终向这些年轻人赔偿了4100万美元。

sentences.en: But what exactly happened during those confessions, Saul?
sentences.zh: 但索尔，在这些供述期间到底发生了什么？

sentences.en: Do we know what happened that prompted the kids to basically make the confessions they did?
sentences.zh: 我们知道是什么导致这些孩子做出这样的供述吗？

sentences.en: Well, we know what the kids say happened.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们知道孩子们是怎么说的。

sentences.en: The kids were in the interrogation rooms for a range of 14 to 30 hours.
sentences.zh: 孩子们在审讯室里待了14到30个小时不等。

sentences.en: The kids say they were threatened, that promises were made.
sentences.zh: 孩子们说他们受到了威胁，对方曾做出承诺。

sentences.en: They believed that by minimizing their involvement,
sentences.zh: 他们相信只要尽量减轻自己的参与程度，

sentences.en: each one I mentioned, nobody confessed to the rape.
sentences.zh: 我提到的每一个人，都没有人承认强奸。

sentences.en: Each one said I played a subsidiary minor role.
sentences.zh: 每个人都说我只起到了次要的、微小的作用。

sentences.en: Each one, upon confession, was arrested,
sentences.zh: 每个人在招供后都被逮捕了，

sentences.en: They thought they were going home.
